scope: Manual qualitative review of three selected LIBERO frames, one prompt and seed each. Not simulator success or policy evaluation.
overall: All three outputs have visible task or scene-preservation problems. These examples do not establish a general failure rate, but do not support using this base checkpoint directly for this run.

drawer_close.observation: Drawer remains visibly open; robot arm is truncated/disconnected and the bottle beside the cabinet disappears.

microwave_close.observation: Microwave door remains open; most of the robot and the unrelated countertop mug disappear, and background framing changes.

pudding_place.observation: Generates an unboxed dessert and an extra plate instead of relocating the existing rectangular pudding package. Robot and mug are largely preserved.

limitations: Public base BAGEL, not the robot-finetuned world model described in the pi0.7 paper.
One static camera; no action or time-horizon conditioning.
Later demo frames were used only for comparison, never as generation inputs. Their offsets are 9.8 to 11.6 seconds and represent subtask endpoints.
Pudding instruction uses task-relative right, which differs from image-right in this camera view.
PyTorch SDPA fallback was checked numerically against explicit attention; equivalence to upstream full-model FlashAttention output was not tested.
All compressed blocks were CPU-offloaded. Latency includes this offload and concurrent GPU jobs; it is not an optimized throughput measurement.
